full_judgment:
2. Respondent as plaintiff filed the aforesaid suit for perpetual injunction against the appellant praying for restraining the defendant and his employees and representatives from using trade mark and copyright similar to that of the plaintiff in the toilet bath soap produced by the defendant. In that suit plaintiff prayed for temporary injunction. Plaintiffs prayer for temporary injunction against the defendant appellant was allowed by the impugned order. 

 1. That the suit having been filed by Md. Anwar Hossain, Administrative Officer (নির্বাহী কর্মকর্তা) of the registered company, Commander Soap Co. Ltd. the suit is not maintainable and the plaintiff has no cause of action for the same. 

 3. That the trade mark of the defendant is not similar to the trade mark of the plaintiff. There are much distinctions, between the two trade marks and ordinary buyers can clearly find out the distinction between the two trade marks and, as such, there is no chance of deception of the ordinary buyer by the use of the trade mark of the defendant. 

 5. It appears from the submission of the learned Advocates of both the parties that written statement in the suit has already been filed by the defendant and the question of maintainability of the suit has clearly been raised in the said written statement. None of the learned Advocates could appraise the court whether any issue regarding maintainability of the suit has been framed or not. But from the written objection it does not appear that such question of maintainability was raised before the trial Court at the time of hearing of the injunction matter. It does not appear from the impugned order that any such question was raised before the court below at the time of hearing the temporary injunction matter. Court is not required to look into maintainability of the suit at the time of hearing of the injunction matter. Maintainability of the suit is to be decided after filing of the written statement and framing of any issue on such point. So I do not find any merit in the contention of the learned Advocate for the appellant that the suit is not maintainable and the court below was not justified in allowing the prayer for temporary injunction. The mistake pointed out by the learned Advocate for the appellant can be corrected at any stage of the suit by amending the cause title of the plaint. So it will not be proper to make any finding on the said question at the stage of the hearing interlocutory injunction matter as the matter was not raised before the court below depriving the plaintiff opportunity to meet such objection. 

 6. In the application for temporary injunction plaintiff prayed for restraining the defendant and his employees and representatives from producing and selling any soap with the trade mark and copyright mentioned in 'Ka' and 'Kha' schedule of the plaint and similar thereto. 

 7. By the impugned order court below restrained the defendant company from using design and get up similar to that of the plaintiff and marketing his products with the same. From the application of temporary injunction and the written objection thereto it is clear that the plaintiff complained that the defendant has been producing soft bath soap using trade mark and copy right similar to that of the plaintiff mentioned in 'Ka' schedule of the plaint through his trade mark and copyright mentioned in 'Kha' schedule of the plaint. Defendant asserted that his trade mark and copyright as mentioned in schedule 'Kha' of the plaint is not similar to the 'Ka' schedule trade mark and copyright of the plaintiff. So defendant clearly understood the purport of the impugned order restraining him from using the trade mark and copyright similar to that of the plaintiff though the ordering portion of the impugned judgment is a bit defective , 

 8. On consideration of the materials on record court below came to the finding that the word "Mosco (মসকো)" used in the soap packet of the defendant is phonetically and visually similar to the word" Cosco (কসকো)" used by the plaintiff in the packet of his soap and can create doubt and deceive and the defendant used similar colour and design of the plaintiff for the said purpose and, as such, plaintiff has prima facie case and balance of convenience and inconvenience in his favour and would suffer irreparable loss and injury. In coming to the aforesaid finding Court below considered the registration of plaintiffs trade mark and copyright mentioning the design and get up of his product "Cosco Soap." Court below further noticed that defendant has recently applied for registration of his trade mark of the soap produced by him and the said application is still pending. Court below also compared the printed packet of "Cosco" of the plaintiff mentioned in 'Ka' schedule of the plaint registered with the colour design and get up as shown therein with the colour design and get up of the defendants printed packet of "Mosco" as shown in the 'Kha" schedule of the plaint and concluded that there are more similarities than dissimilarities between the two. There is no doubt that the names of the Company in the two soap packets are different and on plaintiffs soap packet the words "Cosco Transparent Glycerine Soap" and on defendant's soap packet the words "Mosco Transparent Bath Soap" have been printed. But in respect of colour, design and get up of the two packets no distinction is discernible. On close examination it is noticed that colour and design of the lady and her hair style printed on defendant's soap packet is a bit different from the colour and design of the lady printed on plaintiffs soap packet. There is no distinction in the design of the soap printed in the packet of plaintiffs soap and that of the defendant's soap. Distinctions mentioned above can only be detected by a literate and intelligent person. It would be difficult for an illiterate and ordinary buyer of this country to make any distinction between the two. Moreover, plaintiff has been marketing his soap with trade mark which has been registered on 13th January, 1988. It has been claimed that the plaintiff has been using this trade mark since 1959. It appears from a trade mark registration certificate dated 25.4.61 that Commander Soap Co. had been using trade mark of 'Cosco Glycerine Soap' from 3rd February, 1959 though colour, design and get up of the said trade mark is different from plaintiffs present registered trade mark. It further appears from a copy of the application filed by the defendant on 2nd July, 1993 for registration of his trade mark with the colour, design and get up as mentioned in 'Kha' schedule of the plaint that he has been using the same since 1988. It does not appear from the written objection of the defendant-appellant that he has been using disputed trade mark though unregistered since 1988 as claimed in his application for registration of the said trade mark. 

 9. Mr. Syed Ishtiaq Ahmed, learned Advocate appearing for the respondent, referring to a decision in the case or Iron-Ox Remedy Co. Ltd. vs. Co-Operative Wholesale Society Ltd. printed at page 381 of Trade Mark Case from (1907) 24 RP 6, 425 submitted that the defendant has been taking undue advantage of the long standing business connections and the expenditure incurred by the plaintiff in popularising plaintiffs soap in passing of his goods with a similar name and marks which is likely to mislead the ordinary buyers. On this question learned Advocate for the appellant relied on the case of Dacca Match Factory Ltd. vs. Bangladesh Match Company Ltd. reported in 30 DLR 244. In this case court below as well as the High Court found that there are dissimilarities between the two labels of the plaintiff and the defendant. Both the trade marks are registered trade mark and that plaintiff as well as the defendant company were under the management of the same Corporation for some time when plaintiff company did not raise objection with the user of the defendant's trade marks and they raised objection long after the said company went out of the management of the said corporation. A Division Bench of this Court in that case maintained the order of the trial Court disallowing the prayer for temporary injunction with the following observations: 

 "From the pleadings of the parties and annexures submitted by them and examination of the plaintiffs trade mark as a whole and not merely a particular part of it, namely, the horse mark, the defendant's label does not appear to be identical to the plaintiffs trade mark and there is no confusion at least amongst the dealers of safety matches as to the respective identities of the two contending marks." 

 It is for the court to come to a prima facie decision whether the marks used by the defendant of his product is similar to the marks used by the plaintiff. If in spite of some minor distinctions the Court finds similarity between the two marks on consideration of the materials before it the court is justified to restrain the defendant who is found to be subsequent user of the mark. In this case trial Court after noticing the distinction came to the conclusion that there are some similarities and possibility of deception of the ordinary buyers. I have also noticed the similarities and dissimilarities between the two marks. I have nothing to disagree with the finding of the trial Court in this respect. Moreover, the plaintiff prima facie being owner and earlier user of the trade mark is entitled to restrain the defendant by an order of temporary injunction. In the case of Shafquat Haider vs. Md. AI-Amin reported in 1987 BLD (AD) 130 it has been held that in case of similarity between the two names likely to create confusion in the minds of the customers temporary injunction can be granted to restrain the defendant from passing of his goods as that of the plaintiffs. Here is the case similar to that where the defendant has been trying to pass of his "Mosco Transparent Bath Soap" as that of the plaintiffs "Cosco Transparent Glycerine Soap". I therefore, find no merit in the contentions of the learned Advocate for the appellant.
